title: Tooling: 2.50x faster complete PR589 hosted audit with exact digest
body:
The retained PR589 hosted-owner audit serializes all 7,843,392 mapped instructions from scratch. This opt-in, source-pinned adapter reuses JSON fragments within each invocation while retaining the exact emitted byte stream and the complete inherited audit.

On the same pinned fixture, Python 3.12.3 / macOS arm64:

| Check | Baseline | Adapter | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Instruction digest | 17.417 s | 1.828 s | 9.53x |
| Full hosted audit, including mutations | 25.836 s | 10.325 s | 2.50x |

These are local measurements from one sequential pair, not performance gates or cross-machine guarantees. Both complete audit receipts are byte-identical and match the retained receipt; all 16 inherited mutation checks remain active. The adapter has no persistent cache and refuses changed auditor/parameterizer source bytes or disabled assertions.

Validation passed:
- `python3 -B research/bit-hosted-digest-fastpath/verify.py`: full same-fixture digest and audit comparison, 120 byte-stream comparisons, ten changed-input controls, null-index/source-pin/assertion controls, and all inherited mutants.
- `python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/bit-hosted-digest-fastpath --check-only`: metadata and exact source pins.
- `git diff --cached --check`.

Scope: seven new files under `research/bit-hosted-digest-fastpath/`; frozen inputs, selected frontier and cold-replay driver remain unchanged. This does not rerun the native word, parent audit or outer assembly and claims no new kappa. The registered replay uses only Python 3.12's standard library.

Base: `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`. Verification-engineering seed 91; refined `replay-runtime` card. Final overlap check covered 531 open PRs and 40 recently updated discussions; no matching hashing optimization found. [Claim and handoff](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1871).

Credit: DaysSky (PR442), Chafik Boukhalfa/chafreaky (PR444), DreamingOfClouds (PR463/510/589), eumemic (PR555 and the P111 parameterizer), and the retained community-hyperplane599 audit archive. Prepared by Matthieu Pascal (@mtpsl) with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0.
